eras._note: 2004-2006 static site (Dreamweaver): portfolio.htm lists the companies as links to portfolio_<x>.htm; the featured company links to portfolio.htm itself inside <strong>. 2003's portfolio.html carried Nanoxis alone (also on the 2004 list) and is not configured.
2007-2010 static site: investments.html renders one <div class=item> per company with the logo alt as the name; per-company pages investments_<x>.html.

2010-2013 Umbraco site: /investments lists every company (current and past) as
  • NameCategory
    ; per-company pages /investments/ appear in 2013.
2013-12 to 2016 WordPress site (post type 'investment'): the /investment/ archive lists each company as a link to /investment/<slug>/ wrapping the logo image whose alt is the name.

2017-2023 static React-rendered site: /portfolio renders one <div class=cr-portfolio__item> per company whose only identifier is the logo sprite id (data-logo), alongside data-status, data-type, data-founded, data-invested, data-partner, data-ceo and data-url attributes; no name element exists, so the row's name derives from the slug here and is corrected by the site sources (the live CMS rendering, or sources/site/portfolio-2017-2023.json, which carries the attributes as a file_list source).

2023-09 onward: Nuxt 2 full-static site on Contentful. The server-rendered /commitments HTML carries six highlight names only; the archived _nuxt/static/<build>/commitments/payload.js captures (first build of each year) hold every CMS row (title, slug, date, exited, state, types, creandumLeads) and are decoded through site-portfolio.py's nuxt decoder. Per-company pages /commitments/<slug> are enumerated by the cdx_company_pages era.
eras._builds_note: Build ids read off the CDX index on 2026-09-04 (first archived commitments/payload.js of each year) before the index went down; the replay resolves them when CDX refuses.

roster._note: The CDX roster covers the /team/<first-last> namespaces of 2013-2026 (WordPress, the 2017-2023 static site, Nuxt). The 2004-2013 team pages used first-name files (claes.htm, team_fredrik.html) and one listing page, so the early partners are CURATED into partner-roster.json from the archived team pages (2004, 2008, 2010-2013) with the tenure windows those captures support — see sources/wayback/README.md. The 2017 site's first-name-only slugs (/team/staffan) are dropped by the first-last rule and covered by the full-name slugs of the other eras.

desks._note: Namesakes verified by entity and address (Jakobsbergsgatan 18 Stockholm; 36 Carnaby Street London; 58 S Park St San Francisco), never by name: Creades AB (Nasdaq Stockholm investment company), Creand (Credit Andorra's brand). No namesake files with the SEC under the Creandum name as of 2026-09-04: all eleven CIKs are the firm's own fund vehicles (decisions.md ruling 1).

profile._note: The live CMS 'types' vocabulary (SaaS, Consumer, AI, Fintech, Climate, Health, Other) and the 2017-2023 site's data-type values crosswalk to the closed taxonomy; 'Other' stays unmapped. focus_min_companies ~4.5% of the expected base (PRO-72 Phase 4).

shape._note: Defaults kept: an early-stage, site-listed base is the shape the defaults describe (PRO-72 expects Seed/Series A heavy, Nordic-concentrated, a real C2A cohort). S2A ceiling restated 2026-09-17 under the status contract (D-S2A in decisions.md): 79 seed entries, 8 censored, 34 undetermined, cohort 37 at 83.8% with 52% coverage. Creandum files no Form Ds, so every decision rests on a citation, and on a Nordic book about half the seeds have a reachable published record; the half that does skews to the companies the press followed. Restated to 0.90 with the coverage published beside the rate; the guard still fires above that.
